changes.reason: Sr 4p overlaps the kept O 2s band, so the 4-band cut is not isolated and the gate ignores it. Excluding only Sr 4s gives an isolated cut (15.66 eV gap) and brings Sr 4p in as 3 more functions (num_wann 16, num_bands 51).

diagnosis: The deck cuts out the lowest 4 bands (Sr 4s + Sr 4p) as semicore, but the Sr 4p bands (bands 2-4, -19.3 to -16.8 eV) overlap the O 2s band that is kept (band 5, -17.1 to -15.65 eV). Their gap is -0.35 eV, so they are entangled. The gate does not honour that exclusion, so it scores every excluded occupied state as missing. That alone explains the ~50 % missing occupied states and the 6.4 eV RMS distance, and it explains why all ten frontier runs give the identical 0.4992 / 6.413 no matter what thresholds they used. Projectability thresholds cannot fix a band-index cut. The fix is to move the cut. Sr 4s (band 1, -35 eV) sits 15.66 eV below everything else and is a clean, honoured cut. So exclude only Sr 4s and bring Sr 4p into the construction as three more PAO functions (13 -> 16 functions, num_bands 48 -> 51; validate_deck accepts this). The truncated-eta2 failure probably shares the same cause: the single model band near -16 eV is trying to be O 2s while entangled with Sr 4p, and that band is visibly wiggly in the model band plot. With the 4p/2s block represented in full, the deep bands should be reproduced exactly and the model should become shorter-ranged.
